description:
## What reaches transport that should not

`enum_take_drop_split` fails with (message added by fz-f98.17):

    transport invariant failed: resume payload value ValueId(8) in executable
    ExecutableKey { activation: ActivationKey { function: FunctionId(228), ... } }
    has no analyzed type because the activation is a value template -- a
    value-template activation reached transport and cannot be materialized
    (fz-hwn.23; predicate key_is_value_template)

The executable, probed:

    fn    = List.reduce_while_cont/3
    arrow = ([any], {[a1_0_e], int}, a2) -> r0
    need  = Value
    analysis: 8 known value types, 0 callsites

Every slot is a template: `a2` is a bare, un-instantiated reducer variable and
`r0` an un-instantiated return. No call can supply a bare variable, so the body
analyses nothing (0 callsites) and its delivered values have no types. This is
not a runtime specialization; it is the fz-hwn.23 phantom.

It is PRE-EXISTING. Before fz-f98.17 the same phantom was there, and
`resolve_closure_call` handed its reducer call the earned `any`, which gave the
delivered value a type and let the phantom sail through. Removing that `any`
did not create the phantom -- it stopped hiding it.

## The predicate already exists and is unused

`Types::key_is_value_template` (types/mod.rs:1014) says exactly this:

    /// True when any input position of `key` is a value template -- the key
    /// names an activation that cannot become a runtime/backend executable
    /// because an argument would carry an unrepresentable bare-variable value.

Production call sites: NONE. It has a unit test (types_test.rs:87) and nothing
else. `native.rs:3417` uses the scalar `is_value_template` only to NAME the
failure once a phantom has already reached the backend, and its own comment
says so: "the cure is grounding/pruning the activation before lowering
(fz-hwn.27.8)". The cure was never written.

So this ticket adds no concept. It applies one that is already defined, named,
documented and tested.

## Two placements tested, BOTH FALSIFIED (do not redo them)

1. Prune at the activation mint point -- `prepare_function_call`
   (jobs/semantic.rs), `if world.types().key_is_value_template(arg_types) {
   return None }`:

       cargo test --lib -> 1436 passed / 11 FAILED

   It clears the enum_take_drop_split family but breaks eleven
   capture/closure-boundary tests
   (compiler2_transport_plan_requires_a_boundary_for_an_escaped_lambda,
   compiler2_runtime_demand_marks_an_escaped_callable_first_class,
   compiler2_transport_plan_preserves_capture_lane_order_and_duplicates, ...).
   Too aggressive: a SEMANTIC activation may legitimately carry a template
   argument and ground later. The predicate's own wording is about becoming a
   RUNTIME/BACKEND EXECUTABLE, not about existing as a fact.

2. Prune at `local_call_targets` (jobs/runtime_demand.rs:1299), filtering
   targets whose `activation_inputs` are a value template: this is the right
   LAYER (activation -> ExecutableKey) and it does clear
   enum_take_drop_split, but `local_call_targets` and its two callers
   (`direct_local_targets`, and the delivered-return-demand loop) have no
   `&Types` in scope. Threading it through the demand-cone walk is the actual
   work of this ticket, and was not attempted rather than done badly.

## What to decide first

`local_call_targets` is one of at least three places an activation becomes an
`ExecutableKey` (also jobs/runtime_demand.rs:986, jobs/artifact.rs:1444). Three
placements for one rule is a smell. Find the single chokepoint where an
activation is DEMANDED as a runtime executable and apply the predicate once
there -- or establish that the boundary genuinely has three doors and say why.
Do not sprinkle the check.

## Not the answer

Defaulting the missing type to `any` at the consumer. `resume_payload_ty`'s
sibling arm three lines above it already does exactly that for entry captures:

    facts.analysis().value_types.get(&capture).copied()
        .unwrap_or_else(|| world.types_mut().any())

That is the fz-f98.17 defect, one layer downstream, and it is presumably
hiding the same phantom on the capture path. Auditing it is part of this
ticket.

## Checks

- `enum_take_drop_split` compiles and matches its Elixir oracle on interp, run
  and build; the 4 lib + 3 matrix reds in that family clear.
- `key_is_value_template` has at least one production call site, at one
  boundary, with a comment saying which.
- The `unwrap_or_else(any)` on the entry-capture path is either removed or
  justified in place with evidence that its value can legitimately be absent.
- No new panics: a pruned activation must leave the plan consistent, not
  produce a dangling reference.
- Full lib + matrix at baseline or better.

comments.text:
RESOLVED, and the ticket's own prescription was FALSIFIED on the way. Recording
both so nobody redoes the third placement.

## Placement 3, tried and FALSIFIED: prune at the settled-target boundary

The ticket asked for the single chokepoint where an activation is demanded as a
runtime executable, and there is one: all three doors (runtime_demand.rs:986,
runtime_demand.rs:1299, artifact.rs:944/972) read the same
CallTargetSummary::activation. Collapsed them into
CallTargetSummary::runtime_executable and applied key_is_value_template there.

    cargo test --lib -> 1363 passed / 86 FAILED

Every failure is the same shape:

    compiler2 materialization for root 0: missing transport layout for position
    ExecutableReturn { ... FunctionId(180), arrow: Ty(145) ... }

Probed: the pruned activation IS required by the plan. Value-template
activations are materialized successfully TODAY and produce correct answers --
fn 180 arrow ([a0_e], {:cont, int}, a2) -> r0 is one of them. So
key_is_value_template is NOT the discriminator between "compiles" and "does
not", and the boundary the ticket named is the wrong layer. Pruning there leaves
artifact.rs:1444 still building a call edge to the pruned key: a dangling
reference, exactly the failure mode the ticket's own Checks warned about.

Three placements are now falsified: prepare_function_call (11 red),
local_call_targets/the demand boundary (86 red), and no-Types-in-scope was never
the real obstacle -- the rule simply does not belong at any of them.

## What the probe actually showed

Printing every pruned arrow across both fixtures: EVERY one ends in `-> r0`, and
every one has a bare variable at the reducer slot (a2 / a5). The predicate reads
the SLOT, and the slot is where the truth is. The activation is fine; the
ARGUMENT is unrepresentable.

## The fix: inhabitation, at the callee slot

resolve_closure_call already had the rule one line above the exit fz-f98.17
touched:

    if world.types().is_empty(&callee_ty) || ... {
        // Proven-empty callee or argument: the call site is dead. This is
        // evidence (the empty type), not absence.
        return Ok((None, Some(none_ty(world))));
    }

A bare type variable is the same situation for the same reason: nothing
inhabits it, so the call never happens. Extended the existing dead-call test
rather than adding a branch:

    fn callee_has_no_inhabitants(types: &Types, callee_ty: Ty) -> bool {
        types.is_empty(&callee_ty) || types.is_value_template(&callee_ty)
    }

That is is_value_template's production call site, at one boundary, and it
collapses INTO an existing rule instead of adding one. The callee trichotomy is
now stated once and is three-way: dead (uninhabitable -> none), absent (pending
or un-instantiated -> None, stay subscribed), dynamic edge (ground and
unresolvable -> earned any).

## Second half: a dead call must still lower

With the reducer call dead, the phantom body published no callsite summary, and
materialize_closure_call_edge returned Ok(None) -- leaving native lowering a
ClosureCall tail with a Deliver destination and no return flow:

    native indirect closure call with Deliver destination is missing delivered
    return-flow

Behind the settled materialization gate an absent summary is the Kleene bottom,
exactly as CallTargetSummary::settled_return already reads an absent return. It
now lowers as CallReturnFlow::NoReturn over the empty type -- which is the
existing vocabulary for "never returns", already handled at native.rs:1568.

## Entry-capture audit (the ticket's third Check)

Both entry-capture `unwrap_or_else(any)` sites replaced with a probe panic and
run against the full corpus: ZERO hits across lib (1449) and matrix (416). The
default was dead, so it is now an invariant -- entry_capture_value /
entry_capture_ty, mirroring resume_payload_value / resume_payload_ty. TEN more
any-defaults remain in transport.rs; filed as fz-f98.20, including the sharp one
where the ResumePayload position kind has two derivations that disagree.

## Gates

    lib     1444 passed / 4 failed  ->  1448 passed / 1 failed
    matrix   413 passed / 3 failed  ->   416 passed / 0 failed
    clippy --workspace --all-targets clean, fmt clean

enum_take_drop_split matches its Elixir oracle byte-for-byte on interp, run and
build.

The one remaining lib red is NOT in this family: it is
compiling_the_same_root_twice_publishes_byte_identical_backend_programs on
enum_predicate_search, and decomposing its diff proves the structure is
identical and only raw Ty numbering moved. Filed as fz-f98.19.

title: Value-template activations reach transport: key_is_value_template is defined and unit-tested but never applied in production
